gen-silkscreen-manrope: Silkscreen spaces its blocky little letters so generously you can nearly feel the gaps between them, like retro pixels laid out on a shelf. Manrope follows in a plain sans with open curves.
gen-silkscreen-satoshi: Satoshi is a tall, friendly sans whose wide-open e never looks pinched. Silkscreen is the lo-fi showoff here, while Satoshi does the quiet work of staying easy to follow.
gen-silkscreen-switzer: Strung-out, spaghetti-thin letters give Silkscreen a lo-fi, retro look with room around every character. And Switzer, a tall-waisted sans-serif with wire-like strokes, keeps a long stretch of text moving smoothly.
gen-silkscreen-work-sans: Silkscreen brings a lo-fi, retro look, with space around each letter you can almost feel. But Work Sans, a plain sans with a high mean line, is what makes the pairing feel so current.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-syriac-western: Noto Sans Syriac Western reads modern and clean, its small letters packed with height like bundled cable and terminals held well back from the stroke. Eater adds a dark, stamped bite on top.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Flavors is whimsical and commanding, with towering strokes of zero modulation. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern follows with tall lowercase and curve endings that keep their distance, so paragraphs stay approachable and light.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tc: Loud, round and expressive, Autour One hits hard with no shift from hairline to stem. Noto Sans TC, a plain sans with outward-opening curves, keeps paragraphs easy to move through.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-noto-sans-wanch: Funnel Display draws spaghetti-like strokes of a single width, with c tips that stay well apart. Noto Sans Wancho answers with a hulking lowercase like pressed chalk, so the two feel heavy and loose together.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Audiowide gives a futuristic, tech-minded heading with constant-width arms and legs, like tiles set with wide grout lines. Noto Sans Kannada, a plain sans, suits a larger heading size.
gen-almendra-display-switzer: Almendra Display is ornate and literary, with a pronounced x-height and letters that never pinch shut. Switzer is a plain sans with tubular, wire-like strokes, so give the heading extra size.
